newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Petron poised to revamp image.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Petron poised to revamp image.

text.p: The Philippines' biggest oil refiner, Petron Corp, is set to redefine its corporate structure and public image in the face of growing competition in a newly deregulated industry, Petron officials said on Monday.
"We are embarking on a new image, a new company altogether, one that is more vibrant and professional," Petron chairman Monico Jacob told stockholders at its annual meeting on Monday.
The programme will cost at least 200 million pesos ($7.6 million).
He said the programme would make its service stations more service-oriented and customer-friendly. It will set up 40 new stations and refurbish 40 existing ones this year.

Officials said preliminary talks had started with retail firm Uniwide Holdings Corp to set up convenience stores in its service stations. Fastfood chain Jollibee Foods Corp is also reported to be interested in putting hamburger chains in its stations.
"Shell has done it, Caltex has done it. The environment has changed," president Ali Al-Ajmi said when asked by Reuters what prompted the decision to project a new image.

Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp, a member of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Caltex (Philippines) Inc, a joint venture between Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc are the two other major players in the industry.
Pilipinas Shell was the first to refurbish service stations. Caltex followed suit.

Al-Ajmi said Petron could not remain complacent despite its traditional strengths, such as size and wide network of marketing and distribution facilities and lower freight rates for shipments due to economies of scale.
Petron operates the biggest refinery with a capacity of 160,000 barrels per day (bpd). This will be increased to 180,000 bpd by next year.
Since the full deregulation of the oil industry in February, the Department of Energy said about 35 local and foreign firms had plans to put new oil marketing and storage facilities.
For the year, Petron has earmarked 5.4 billion pesos in capital expenditure, the bulk of which will go on marketing and distribution expenses, Al-Ajmi said.

Despite the increased competition, Al-Ajmi said he expected Petron to improve its sales volume by more than the six percent annual industry average, raising its market share higher than 41.4 percent in 1996.
"We have been threatened but we are defending our position. We have not lost an account," Rafael Diaz, Petron industrial trade manager told shareholders.
Jacob said the company would soon dominate the sector in the reseller market. Petron's market share in the gasoline market has reached 33.4 percent as of February this year from 30.9 percent in 1993.
He said the company had created a business development department to explore new investment opportunities.
Al-Ajmi said Petron cut manpower last year by 25 percent to 1,269 from 1,686 previously to make it on a par with the competition.
"We wanted Petron to have the agility of a small company and the strength of a big one," Al-Ajmi said. (US$1 = 26.30 pesos)
